quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking and skidding.
Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads are worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking and skidding.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). ABS stops the wheels from locking and skidding when you brake hard. It works by releasing and re-applying brake pressure to keep your wheels moving and maintain the best braking power.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are stronger than using either one alone.
The effects are safer than using either one alone.
The effects cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. When these drugs are mixed with alcohol, the danger increases greatly.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black words or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How often does a motorcycle need maintenance compared to a car?

options.text: Only when a mechanic checks it.

questions.correctAnswerText: More often than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, rest for at least two hours to avoid getting too tired.

questions.question: What does an approved helmet do?

options.text: Lets you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision. Any U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet lets you see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look in your blind spot.
Slow down so vehicles can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where should you ride when following another vehicle?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
On the left side of the lane.
Near the right edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Do not worry about other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which item does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A tight baseball cap
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Guarantees you will not be arrested for drinking and riding
Guarantees your riding skills will not be affected
Is fine as long as you ride slowly
May not fully remove alcohol from your body

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. The time needed varies by person. It is safest not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Night riding is usually:

options.text: Easier than day riding because you can see other vehicle lights better
Harder than day riding because visibility is reduced

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than day riding because visibility is reduced
questions.explanation: Night riding is challenging because it is harder to see and be seen. Without normal shadows and light, it is difficult to judge distances.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The seat fabric
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your rims and spokes for bending or damage, tire condition and tread, and all lights. Seat fabric does not affect safe riding.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle
Should not be operated in curves
Should use the shoulder when taking a curve

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars corner differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: To help others see you, wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes you more visible to other drivers. Wear clothes that increase your visibility day and night.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in bright daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect the face as well as goggles

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects the eyes and face
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough protection. A windshield may reduce the requirement for eye protection, but a face shield is still recommended.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot
Be worn for a better grip on the handgrips
Not be worn because they make control harder
Be worn only on cool days

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn for a better grip on the handgrips
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: New riders who don't know their motorcycle well have more crashes.

questions.question: Alcohol doesn't need to be digested like food. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches your brain and affects you within minutes of drinking it.
Alcohol stays in your body forever.
It takes a long time to feel drunk.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches your brain and affects you within minutes of drinking it.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your blood quickly without needing digestion. It reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a motorcycle you've never used?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike because all motorcycles are the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where everything is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes first.

questions.question: What is the minimum fine for riding without proof of insurance?
questions.explanation: Hawaii requires motorcycle liability insurance. You can be fined at least $100 if you don't have proof of insurance.

questions.question: What are intersections?

options.text: Places where crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Places where crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most potential for crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles. Ride carefully through intersections.
